name: Sun acupuncture for CP/CPPS
question: Does acupuncture improve symptoms more than sham acupuncture in men with moderate to severe chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome?

design.blinding: Participants, outcome assessors, and statisticians blinded; acupuncturists unblinded
design.population: 440 men aged 18 to 50 years with moderate to severe chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome (NIH-CPSI at least 15) at ten tertiary hospitals in China.
design.locator: Full text, Methods, Setting and Participants, p 1358; Figure 1, p 1359

verdictNote: Prespecified responder tests were significant at weeks 8 and 32 in intention-to-treat analysis.
takeaway: Among 440 men with moderate to severe chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome, 20 acupuncture sessions over 8 weeks increased modeled NIH-CPSI response versus sham at weeks 8 and 32 (adjusted OR 2.6 at both time points).

reports.label: Primary report
reports.citation: Sun Y, Liu Y, Liu B, et al. "Efficacy of Acupuncture for Chronic Prostatitis/Chronic Pelvic Pain Syndrome: A Randomized Trial." *Ann Intern Med.* 2021;174(10):1357-1366. doi:10.7326/M21-1814
reports.followUp: 8-week treatment; assessment at weeks 8 and 32 (24 weeks after treatment)
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Methods, Interventions and Assessments and Outcomes, pp 1358–1359

results.measure: Week-8 modeled intention-to-treat probability of at least a 6-point NIH-CPSI reduction; n=220 randomized per arm
results.note: Prespecified baseline-adjusted logistic mixed model; withdrawals without NIH-CPSI scores counted as nonresponders. Post hoc adjusted risk difference 21.6 percentage points (95% CI 12.8–30.4).
results.locator: Full text, Statistical Analysis, p 1362; Table 2, pp 1361–1362; Results, p 1363

results.measure: Week-32 modeled intention-to-treat probability of at least a 6-point NIH-CPSI reduction; n=220 randomized per arm
results.note: Prespecified baseline-adjusted logistic mixed model; withdrawals without NIH-CPSI scores counted as nonresponders. Post hoc adjusted risk difference 21.1 percentage points (95% CI 12.2–30.1).
results.locator: Full text, Statistical Analysis, p 1362; Table 2, pp 1361–1362; Results, p 1363

results.measure: Week-8 adjusted mean change from baseline, intention-to-treat; n=220 randomized per arm
results.note: Positive difference denotes greater symptom-score reduction with acupuncture; secondary comparisons were exploratory without multiplicity adjustment.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2, pp 1361–1362; Statistical Analysis, p 1362

results.measure: Week-32 adjusted mean change from baseline, intention-to-treat; n=220 randomized per arm
results.note: Positive difference denotes greater symptom-score reduction with acupuncture; secondary comparisons were exploratory without multiplicity adjustment.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2, pp 1361–1362; Statistical Analysis, p 1362

values.exp: Twenty 30-minute sessions over 8 weeks: three weekly for 4 weeks, then two weekly for 4 weeks
values.ctl: Twenty 30-minute sessions over 8 weeks: three weekly for 4 weeks, then two weekly for 4 weeks

values.exp: Certified acupuncturists with five years of undergraduate training and at least two years of clinical experience
values.ctl: Certified acupuncturists with five years of undergraduate training and at least two years of clinical experience

values.exp: Bilateral BL33 and BL35 to 50–60 mm; BL23 and SP6 to 25–30 mm; manipulation every 10 minutes except at BL33
values.ctl: Superficial 2–3 mm insertion at bilateral nonacupoints lateral to the active sites, without manipulation

values.ctl: 208/220 randomized completed eight-week treatment; mean 19.1 sessions (SD 3.5)
